findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing grant provider factories
findings.body: Adding getShortcut() as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a source/binary incompatible change for every custom grant provider compiled against the old interface. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances and calls getShortcut(), so an existing provider will throw AbstractMethodError at server startup. Provide a default method or handle missing/unsupported values explicitly.

findings.title: getShortcut() contract does not enforce exactly two characters required by the token ID parser
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hardcodes a six-character context and splits it into three two-character pieces, and getTokenContextFromTokenId() rejects prefixes whose length is not 6. The new getShortcut() contract only says 'usually like 3-letters' and does not require a non-null two-character value. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut produces an access-token jti that the decoder rejects with 'Expected length of 6'; returning null makes ConcurrentHashMap.put throw during postInit. Validate non-null/two-character shortcuts at startup or make the encoding self-delimiting.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check is missing and grantType check is duplicated
findings.body: The constructor checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is accepted and then string-concatenated into a jti ending in ':null', while a null grantType throws the misleading message about rawTokenId. The second Objects.requireNonNull call should check rawTokenId.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: The matcher extracts items[0].substring(3, 5), which is not the grant-shortcut position in the six-character prefix (grant is at [4, 6]), and it returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut instead of true. As written it never verifies the grant type and passes any prefixed token with a UUID suffix, so the updated integration tests cannot catch wrong grant encoding. It can also throw if the prefix is shorter than five characters. Fix both the offset and the comparison, and validate the prefix length.

findings.title: Removal of public Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API
findings.body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor is removed by this change. Existing extensions or tests that use it to create a copied context will fail to compile, and precompiled callers will fail to link. If removal is not intentional, keep the constructor and copy the new grantType field as well; otherwise the compatibility break should be explicitly documented.
